import re from typing import List # Compile the regex once to avoid recompilation on every call. # The pattern matches an opening `<`, then any characters that are not `>`, # and finally a closing `>`; the `?` makes it non‑greedy. _TAG_RE = re.compile(r"<[^>]+?>", flags=re.IGNORECASE) def extract_html_tags(html_string: str) -> List[str]: """ Return a list of all HTML tags found in *html_string*. Parameters ---------- html_string : str The input string containing HTML markup. Returns ------- List[str] A list of tags, including the angle brackets (e.g. "
", ""). Notes ----- * The function is defensive: it returns an empty list if the input is not a string. * The regex is deliberately simple to avoid catastrophic backtracking (CWE‑407). """ if not isinstance(html_string, str): return [] # Find all non‑overlapping matches return _TAG_RE.findall(html_string)
